clause: Ch.4 4.17(a)-(d); the per-product and per-batch-size rule sits in the unnumbered lead-in to the Manufacturing Formula and Processing Instructions section
requirement: For every product and every batch size made, an approved written manufacturing formula and processing instructions must exist. The formula names the product with a product code tied to its specification; gives the dosage form, strength and batch size; lists each starting material and its amount, noting any substance that may be lost during processing; and states the expected final yield with its acceptable range, plus relevant intermediate yields where applicable.
system_implications: Master recipe entity keyed by product code + batch size (or an explicitly approved set of discrete sizes); no ad-hoc scaling at batch creation. Bill of materials with quantity per batch and a 'removed during processing' flag (tablets: granulation water/ethanol; injectables: WFI removed by lyophilisation, process gases such as nitrogen used for blanketing; an overage is not a lost substance - any registered overage is part of the stated quantity and must match the MA). Mandatory expected final yield with acceptable limits; expected yields at configured intermediate stages where applicable (limits on intermediate yields are good practice, not demanded by 4.17(d); significant yield deviations are handled under Ch.5 5.44). Only masters in Approved/Effective status can be instantiated. The per-product and per-batch-size rule covers the processing instructions too, so the processing master is keyed the same way.
note: No substantive change. Clause refined: the 'each product and batch size' rule is in the lead-in paragraph before 4.17 and also applies to processing instructions. Implications: 'declared overages' removed as an example of a disappearing substance (an overage is part of the stated amount); limits are only demanded for the final yield, so intermediate-yield limits are relabelled good practice.

requirement: Processing instructions must state where processing takes place and the main equipment; give, or refer to, the methods for readying critical equipment (e.g., cleaning, assembly, calibration, sterilisation); require a pre-start check that equipment and workstation hold no earlier products and no documents or materials unneeded for this process, and that equipment is clean and fit for use; set out detailed ordered steps (material checks, pre-treatment, order of addition, critical parameters such as time and temperature); give in-process control instructions with limits; where needed, define bulk storage requirements (container, labelling, special conditions); and list any special precautions.
system_implications: Master step model must carry: room/area and equipment class; equipment-preparation prerequisites evaluated at run time (clean status and clean-hold expiry, calibration due date, assembly check, sterilisation status and sterile-hold expiry for injectables); a mandatory pre-start clearance step confirming removal of previous products, of documents and of materials not needed for this process, and that equipment is clean and fit for use; ordered steps with CPP set-points and ranges; IPC definitions with limits; bulk hold definitions (container type, label, storage condition, maximum hold time); precaution text shown and acknowledged at the step. Tablets: granulation end-point, drying temperature/LOD, compression force/hardness. Injectables: SIP/autoclave cycle, filter integrity, bulk solution hold time. Verifier: 4.18 requires the instructions to contain these elements; run-time enforcement of clean-hold/sterile-hold expiry and calibration due dates, maximum bulk hold times, and blocking masters whose CPPs lack a range go beyond 4.18 (supported by Ch.4 4.31 logbooks, Ch.5 and, for sterile products, Annex 1) - keep as design choices. Only the equipment-preparation methods may be incorporated by reference (4.18(b)).
note: No substantive change; paraphrase tightened: the clearance check also covers documents and materials not needed for the planned process (not only leftovers), and 'by reference' is allowed only for equipment-preparation methods (4.18(b)). Implications: run-time controls labelled as beyond the clause; clearance scope added.

requirement: Approved packaging instructions must exist for each product, pack size and pack type, containing or referencing: product name with bulk and finished batch numbers; dosage form, and strength where applicable; pack content by number, weight or volume; a complete packaging-material list with quantities, sizes, types and specification codes; where appropriate, specimens of printed materials showing where batch number and shelf-life are to be applied; line-clearance checks and a careful pre-start examination of area and equipment, plus other special precautions; a description of the packaging operation including significant ancillary operations and equipment; and in-process controls with sampling instructions and acceptance limits.
system_implications: Packaging master keyed by product + pack size + pack type, versioned and approved separately from the processing master. Component BOM with item codes linked to approved specifications and artwork versions; artwork specimen image stored with coding/expiry print zones; mandatory line-clearance checklist template; operation steps with equipment classes; IPC plans with sample size, frequency and limits. Batch record must hold both the bulk batch number consumed and the finished-goods batch number. Tablets: blister/bottle counts, desiccant, leaflet. Injectables: vial/ampoule labels, cartons. Safety features (unique identifier and anti-tampering device) apply to most prescription medicines - tablets and injectables alike - under Directive 2011/62/EU and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161; they are not a Ch.4 requirement but belong in the packaging master where the product is in scope. Verifier: printed-material specimens are required only 'where appropriate' (4.19(e)), so allow a justified 'not applicable' rather than a hard block for every printed component.
note: No substantive change. Implications: serialisation/anti-tampering stem from the Falsified Medicines Directive and Delegated Reg. 2016/161 (both tablets and injectables if prescription-only), not Ch.4; printed specimens are 'where appropriate'.

requirement: A batch processing record must be kept for every batch processed, derived from the applicable sections of the formula and processing instructions currently approved. It captures: product name and batch number; start, key intermediate stage and completion dates and times; who carried out each significant step and, where appropriate, who checked it; for each starting material its batch and/or QC control number and the quantity actually weighed, plus the lot and quantity of any recovered or reprocessed material that was added; relevant processing operations or events and the main equipment used; in-process control results with the identity of whoever performed them; yields at relevant stages; notes on special problems with signed authorisation of any departure from the formula or instructions; and approval by the person responsible for processing.
system_implications: Batch record instance is generated only from the effective master version and stamps that version ID. Automatic server-time stamps at step start/stop and stage milestones. Per-step performer e-signature plus configurable second-person verification. Material consumption captured by lot scan and balance integration (actual weight, not keyed-in theoretical), with a distinct flag and source-batch reference for recovered/reprocessed material. Equipment ID captured per step. IPC results entered against limits with performer ID. Stage and final yields auto-calculated. Deviations linked to the step with authorised signature. Final 'production approval' signature role gates hand-over to QA/QP review. Verifier: also record the QC/analytical control number where that, rather than a batch number, identifies the material (4.20(d)). Scale/scanner capture is a design choice - Annex 11 §6 equally accepts a second-person check of manually entered critical data. Blocking production approval while steps are open or deviations unsigned is good practice beyond 4.20. Deviation authorisation should follow Ch.5 5.15 (competent person, QC involved where appropriate).
note: No substantive change; paraphrase reworded. Implications: beyond-clause controls labelled; analytical control number added.

requirement: Where a process has been validated and is subject to continuous monitoring and control, the batch reports the system generates automatically can be cut down to compliance summaries plus exception and out-of-specification reports.
system_implications: Support review-by-exception: a per-batch compliance summary and an exception report listing every out-of-range value, alarm, override, manual entry, correction, deviation and audit-trail change. Only steps configured (under change control, referencing the validation) as validated and continuously monitored may use summary-only reporting; full underlying data is still captured, retained and viewable on drill-down. Verifier: the Note is a permission (reports may be limited), not an obligation, and it does not relax 4.20 content for manually executed steps. Retaining the full underlying data is not stated in the Note itself; it follows from the raw-data definition in the Ch.4 preamble (see EUA-NEW-01) and 4.10/4.12. Listing manual entries, corrections and audit-trail events in the exception report goes beyond the Note (good practice, consistent with 4.27 and Annex 11 §8.2/§9).
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: clarified that raw-data retention comes from the Ch.4 preamble, and that the Note is optional and limited to validated, continuously monitored processes.

requirement: Every batch or part-batch that is packed needs its own batch packaging record, derived from the applicable parts of the packaging instructions. It holds: product name and batch number; dates and times of packaging; who performed each significant step and, where appropriate, who checked it; identity and conformity checks against the instructions, including in-process results; details of the operations with references to the equipment and lines used; where possible, samples of the printed components actually used, with specimens of the batch code, expiry date and any extra overprint; notes on special problems or unusual events with signed authorisation of departures from the instructions; the amounts and identity of every printed component and of the bulk that were issued, consumed, destroyed or sent back to stock, and the amount of finished product obtained, enough for reconciliation; and approval by the person responsible for packaging.
system_implications: Packaging record supports part-batch (sub-lot) records linked to one bulk lot. Captures line ID and equipment IDs, IPC results, and an attached specimen of printed material (scanned sample or vision-system image of the actual coded item). Reconciliation table per printed component and bulk: issued, used, destroyed, returned, plus finished units, samples and rejects. Final approval signature by packaging-responsible role. Verifier: an image is an interpretation of 'samples'; the literal expectation is a physical specimen whenever possible, which an eBMR can keep as a controlled physical attachment cross-referenced to the electronic record (hybrid control per 4.1) - support both. Investigating reconciliation discrepancies before release comes from Ch.5 5.61, not 4.21.
note: No substantive change; paraphrase reworded. Implications: clarified physical versus image specimens and where discrepancy investigation comes from.

requirement: The reconciliation data described in 4.21(h) - identity and quantities of printed materials and bulk issued, used, destroyed or returned, and the product quantity obtained - may be left out of the packaging record only where robust electronic controls operate during packaging and the omission is justified.
system_implications: Reconciliation is ON by default for every packaging master. Turning it off for a component requires a controlled configuration change that names the electronic control relied on (e.g. 100% code/vision verification with verified reject, roll-fed labels with splice detection, serialization aggregation), references its validation, and is approved by QA. The record then shows the justification reference instead of counts. Serialized injectable/tablet packs: reconcile commissioned vs. decommissioned vs. shipped serial numbers as the electronic equivalent. Verifier: the serial-number reconciliation 'equivalent' is an interpretation (serialisation derives from Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161), not something Ch.4 states. The exemption only changes what must appear in the record: significant discrepancies must still be investigated before release (Ch.5 5.61) and unused batch-coded materials destroyed with a record (Ch.5 5.62).
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: serialisation equivalence labelled as interpretation; added the Ch.5 limits on what the exemption relaxes.

requirement: Documentation may be paper, electronic or photographic and the same rules apply to every medium; the document types and media used must be defined in the QMS and followed. Complex systems must be understood, well documented, validated and adequately controlled. For hybrid and single-medium systems alike, the relationships and controls between masters, official copies, data processing and resulting records must be stated; electronic templates, forms and masters need appropriate controls; and record integrity must be assured for the whole retention period.
system_implications: eBMR must declare, per record type, which is the official (master) record: electronic record, printout, or combination. Hybrid points (e.g. printed labels, paper chart recorder output, instrument printouts, paper deviation forms) must be formally mapped with a documented linkage (scan attached as true copy, ID cross-reference). Templates/forms in the system are version-controlled, approved and locked. System is validated (Annex 11) and its configuration controlled. Verifier: 'true copy' is EMA data-integrity Q&A / PIC/S PI 041 terminology rather than Ch.4 wording; fine as a design means.
note: No change.

requirement: Documents must be carefully designed, drafted, reviewed and issued, and must agree, as appropriate, with the relevant parts of the Product Specification File (investigational products) and of the manufacturing and marketing authorisation dossiers. Making working copies from masters must not be able to introduce errors. Instruction documents must be approved, signed and dated by suitably authorised people and have a defined effective date; every document must have unambiguous content and be uniquely identifiable. Instruction documents should be orderly and easy to check, with style and language suited to their use; SOPs, work instructions and methods specifically must use an imperative, mandatory style.
system_implications: Batch record instances are generated programmatically from the approved master (no copy/retype). Master recipe workflow: author -> reviewer(s) -> approver with e-signatures, unique document ID + version, and an effective-from date after which it becomes executable. Mandatory regulatory cross-reference on each master (MA dossier section / variation number; PSF reference for investigational products) confirmed at approval - 4.2 expects compliance with the dossiers, so this should not be optional. Instructions rendered as numbered imperative steps. Verifier: unique identification applies to every controlled document and template, not only instructions (4.3). The imperative-style rule targets SOPs, work instructions and methods (4.4); step text should in any case be orderly and easy to check.
note: MINOR correction: the paraphrase omitted the manufacturing authorisation dossier, limited 'unambiguous / uniquely identifiable' to instruction documents (4.3 applies it to all documents), and extended the imperative-style rule to all instructions (4.4 limits it to SOPs, work instructions and methods). Implications: the MA cross-check should be mandatory, not optional.

clause: Ch.4 4.5 (periodic review only); superseded-version control rests on 4.3 (effective date) and 4.20/4.21 (records based on currently approved instructions)
requirement: Documents in the quality management system must be reviewed regularly and kept current (4.5). Superseded instructions must not be usable for new batches; in the 2011 text this follows from 4.3 (a defined effective date) and 4.20/4.21 (records based on the currently approved instructions), not from 4.5.
system_implications: Masters carry a periodic review due date with alerts; upon approval of a new version the prior version is automatically retired for new batches. Defined rule for batches in progress when a master changes (continue on old version with justification or migrate under change control) and the record shows which version governed each step. Printed forms or labels from superseded versions are invalidated (version/ID printed on every output). Verifier: keep superseded-version blocking - it is required by 4.3 (defined effective date), 4.20/4.21 (records based on the currently approved instructions) and Annex 11 §10, even though the 2011 wording of 4.5 does not mention it.
note: MODERATE (source) correction: the 'prevent inadvertent use of superseded documents' sentence is not in the 2011 text of 4.5; it matches the pre-2011 Chapter 4 wording. The eBMR should still implement it because 4.3, 4.20/4.21 and Annex 11 §10 lead to the same outcome. Implications unchanged.

requirement: Controlled documents should not be handwritten, but documents that call for data entry must leave enough room for the entries; any handwritten entry must be clear, legible and indelible.
system_implications: Every data point in the master has a defined, typed entry field (unit, precision, allowed range or list) so free-text is the exception. Where paper remains (hybrid printouts, emergency paper fallback forms), the printed form is generated from the approved master with enough space for each entry, carries a unique form ID, and is later reconciled into the electronic record. No handwritten master instructions. Verifier: typed fields are the electronic analogue of 'sufficient space' (design). Counting issued fallback forms and reconciling their return is data-integrity good practice (EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity; PIC/S PI 041), not stated in 4.6/4.7 - keep.
note: No change.

requirement: Records must be made or completed as each action is taken, and in a manner that keeps every significant manufacturing activity traceable.
system_implications: Timestamps come from a synchronised server clock, never from a user-editable field. Steps are signed at completion; late entries are allowed only via a 'late entry' path that records actual time of activity, time of entry and a mandatory reason, and are flagged for review. Batch-level genealogy links materials, equipment, rooms, people and steps. Verifier: server-clock time stamps and the late-entry path are design means (supported by Annex 11 §12.4); 4.8 itself sets the contemporaneous-recording and traceability outcome.
note: No change.

clause: Ch.4 4.9 (mandatory reason for GMP-relevant electronic data comes from Annex 11 §9)
requirement: Any alteration to an entry must be signed and dated and must leave the original information readable; where appropriate the reason must also be recorded.
system_implications: Corrections never overwrite: the system keeps original value, new value, who, when (server time) and a mandatory reason (pick-list plus free text) in a secure audit trail. Corrections to GMP-relevant data after step sign-off require re-signature and, for critical data (weights, IPC results, CPPs, yields), a second-person or QA approval. Correction history is shown inline in the batch record view and in the exception report. Verifier: 4.9 asks for a reason only 'where appropriate'; making it mandatory for GMP-relevant electronic data is justified by Annex 11 §9. Second-person/QA approval of corrections to critical data is good practice beyond both texts.
note: No change to the requirement.

requirement: It must be clearly defined which record belongs to each manufacturing activity and where that record is kept, and secure controls - validated where appropriate - must protect record integrity for the entire retention period.
system_implications: Record-type register inside the system (or linked SOP) mapping each activity to its record and storage location (eBMR DB, archive, attached external systems such as SCADA/historian, LIMS, weighing). Integrity controls: role-based write access, audit trail, backup/restore tested, checksums on archived records, readable-format migration plan. Archive/export produces complete human-readable batch record with metadata and audit trail. Verifier: the listed integrity controls are design means that also serve Annex 11 §7.1, §4.8 and §17.
note: No change.

requirement: Batch documentation must be kept for one year after the batch expires or at least five years after QP certification of the batch, whichever is longer. For investigational medicinal products it must be kept at least five years after the last clinical trial using the batch is completed or formally discontinued. Legislation for particular product types (e.g., ATMPs) may require longer periods for some documents.
system_implications: Retention engine computes a retention-until date per batch = max(expiry + 1 year, QP certification date + 5 years), stored with the record and recomputed if expiry is extended/changed; IMP batches use a separate rule tied to trial end dates entered by QA; configurable overrides for longer national or product-type rules. Purge/delete of batch records is impossible before that date and requires QA-approved, audit-trailed disposition afterwards. Retention applies to the full record including audit trails, attachments and linked data (e.g. historian extracts). Verifier (gap): 4.11 is keyed to expiry and QP certification, so define a QA rule for batches never certified (rejected, destroyed or abandoned) and identify validation or stability batches whose records also fall under 4.12.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: added handling for batches that are never certified (not addressed by 4.11).

requirement: Retention of other documentation depends on the business activity it supports. Critical documentation, including raw data (e.g., validation or stability) that supports information in the marketing authorisation, must be kept while the authorisation remains in force. Some of it may be retired once superseded by a complete new data set, with a documented justification that respects batch-record retention; for example, process validation raw data must be kept for no less time than the records of all batches whose release relied on that validation.
system_implications: Masters, master versions, recipe change history, and any validation-linked configuration (e.g. the validated state that justifies review-by-exception) are retained at least as long as any batch record that relied on them. Link each batch to the master version and validation references so retention of those objects is automatically extended while dependent batches are retained. Verifier: keeping master versions as long as dependent batch records is an inference from 4.10/4.12 (a batch record cannot be interpreted without its governing instructions) - sound design, not an explicit rule. Also mark batch records that are critical documentation supporting the MA (e.g., process validation or stability batches) so they are kept while the MA is in force.
note: No change to the requirement.

requirement: Written release and rejection procedures must exist for materials and products, in particular for QP certification of finished product for sale. The QP must have access to every record, and a system must be in place to highlight special observations and any change to critical data.
system_implications: QP/QA review workspace that exposes the complete batch record plus linked deviations, change controls, lab results and audit trails. Automatic flags for special observations (comments, events, deviations) and for any post-entry change to data classified as critical, so the reviewer sees them without searching. Release status workflow: quarantine -> production approved -> QA reviewed -> QP certified / rejected, each with e-signature. Verifier: only the QP certification step must be an e-signature (Annex 11 §15); e-signing the other workflow states, and blocking certification until each flag is acknowledged, are good practice. Rejection must be supported for materials and intermediates as well as finished batches.
note: No change.

requirement: Major or critical production and analytical equipment, and rooms where product is processed, need logbooks that record in time order, as appropriate, each use of the area or equipment/method and any calibration, maintenance, cleaning or repair, with dates and the identity of the people who did it.
system_implications: Electronic equipment and room logbooks that are automatically populated from batch execution (usage start/stop with batch and product ID, cleaning events) and from maintenance/calibration modules; entries are chronological and immutable (corrections per EU4-13). Batch step checks equipment/room status from the logbook (last product, clean status, calibration due). Injectables: also autoclave/SIP cycles, filter integrity tests, isolator/RABS decontamination. Tablets: compression machine tooling (punch/die sets) usage. Verifier: filter integrity results belong in the batch record (4.20(f)) rather than the logbook; logbook-driven status checks at batch steps go beyond 4.31 but support 4.18(c) and 4.20(e). 4.31 also covers major/critical analytical equipment, usually handled in LIMS rather than the eBMR.
note: No change.

clause: Ch.4 4.3; 4.9; 4.13; 4.20(c),(f),(h),(i); 4.21(c),(g),(i); 4.31; e-signature properties Annex 11 §14, QP certification §15
requirement: Chapter 4 signature/identification points: instruction documents approved, signed and dated by authorised persons (4.3); specifications authorised and dated (4.13); alterations signed and dated (4.9); processing and packaging records identify who performed each significant step and, where appropriate, who checked it (4.20(c), 4.21(c)), and who performed in-process controls (4.20(f)); departures from instructions carry signed authorisation (4.20(h), 4.21(g)); the responsible person approves the completed processing or packaging record (4.20(i), 4.21(i)); logbooks identify who carried out each operation (4.31). Annex 11 §14, now checked, lets these be electronic signatures that carry the weight of handwritten ones inside the company, stay permanently linked to the record and show date and time; §15 requires QP certification by e-signature.
system_implications: Signature catalogue built into the product with one configurable signature type per point: master approval, correction, step performed, step verified, deviation authorisation, production/packaging record approval, QA review, QP certification. Each type defines the allowed roles, whether the signer must differ from earlier signers on the same object, and whether re-authentication is needed. Every signature event is recorded in the audit trail and shown in the rendered record. Verifier: add signature types for IPC performer (4.20(f)), specification approval if specifications are held in the system (4.13) and logbook entries (4.31). Every e-signature must carry date and time and be permanently bound to its record (Annex 11 §14). Signature 'meaning' and re-authentication at each signing come from 21 CFR Part 11 (11.50, 11.200), not the 2011 EU texts - keep for dual-market use.
note: MINOR correction: added missed identification points (IPC performer 4.20(f), specification authorisation 4.13, logbook identity 4.31) and replaced the 'Annex 11 not re-checked' caveat with the verified §14/§15 content.

clause: Ch.4 Principle and preamble 'Required GMP documentation' (Records definition); see also 4.28 (distribution records to support recall)
requirement: 'Written' means recorded or documented on any medium from which data can be rendered human-readable. Records provide evidence of actions taken and, for manufactured batches, a history of each batch including its distribution (4.28 adds that distribution records must allow recall of any batch). Controls must keep documents accurate, intact, available and legible.
system_implications: Every electronic batch record, including its metadata, attachments and audit trail, can be rendered on demand as a complete human-readable report (screen and PDF/print) for inspectors and the QP, for the whole retention period. The batch genealogy can be linked to distribution data held in ERP, so the history of a batch can be traced forward to customers for recall.
note: No change; clause refined (the records definition sits in the 'Required GMP documentation' preamble; 4.28 is the specific distribution-record clause). The researcher's verified=false can now be treated as verified. The raw-data sentence of the same preamble is not covered by any line - added as EUA-NEW-01.

requirement: Annex 11 covers every computerised system used in GMP-regulated activities. The application must be validated and the IT infrastructure qualified. Replacing a manual operation with a computerised system must not reduce product quality, process control or quality assurance, and must not raise the overall risk of the process.
system_implications: Every control that exists in the paper BMR (line clearance sign-off, second-person checks, yield reconciliation, label reconciliation, in-process checks) needs an equivalent electronic control in the eBMR, or a documented risk-based justification that overall process risk does not rise (the Principle judges the overall outcome rather than demanding control-by-control equivalence; e.g., Ch.4 4.21(h) lets robust electronic controls replace reconciliation data). The vendor/customer must be able to deliver validation evidence for the configured application (recipes, workflows, calculations, interfaces) and qualification evidence for servers, database, network and any cloud tenancy.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: 'equal or stronger control per paper control' overstates the Principle; reframed as an equivalent control or a risk-justified alternative.

requirement: Risk management must be applied across the system's whole life cycle, weighing patient safety, data integrity and product quality; how far validation and data-integrity controls go must be decided on a justified, documented risk assessment of the system.
system_implications: The eBMR should let the regulated user tag each data field / step with a criticality class (e.g., critical process parameter, GMP-relevant, informational) and drive controls from that tag: second-person verification, mandatory reason-for-change, audit-trail review flags, and exception reporting. The risk assessment behind the classification must be stored/linked as a controlled document. Injectables will typically classify more steps as critical (aseptic interventions, sterilisation, filtration, environmental monitoring excursions) than tablets. Verifier: criticality tagging is a design means, not required by §1, but it is a practical way to evidence the risk basis that §1, §6 and §9 call for.
note: No change.

requirement: A current inventory listing every relevant computerised system and the GMP functions it performs must be available. For critical systems there must also be a current description covering the physical and logical set-up, how data flow, the interfaces to other systems or processes, hardware and software prerequisites, and the security measures.
system_implications: The regulated user is accountable for the inventory and description; the eBMR vendor should supply (and keep current per release) an architecture/system description: modules, database, integration points (ERP/material management, LIMS, weighing scales, SCADA/PLC, historian, label printers, QMS for deviations), data flow diagrams, and security design. The system should be able to export its own configuration inventory (interfaces enabled, versions) to help keep the description current. Verifier: the site inventory must also list the connected systems themselves (scales, PLC/SCADA, LIMS, printers, vision systems), each with its GMP function.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: the obligation sits with the regulated user (vendor documentation supports it); connected systems added to the inventory.

requirement: When data are moved into a different format or a different system, the validation must verify that neither their values nor their meaning change during that migration.
system_implications: Upgrades, database migrations, archive exports and legacy-record imports must include automated reconciliation: record counts, checksums/hashes per record, field-level comparison of values and units, and preservation of audit trail, signatures and metadata. Signature manifestations and audit-trail links must survive migration and remain bound to the same records. Verifier: §4.8 requires the checks, not that they be automated (automation is a design choice). Preserving signature linkage follows from §14 (permanently linked).
note: No change.

requirement: Critical data keyed in by hand need an additional accuracy check, either by a second person or by a validated electronic check; risk management must address how critical the data are and what wrong or mistaken entries could cause.
system_implications: For fields classified critical (e.g., dispensed weight typed manually, lot number of an API, compression force set-point, fill volume/weight, sterilisation cycle parameters, filter integrity test result), the eBMR must either (a) capture the value directly from the instrument/scale/PLC or verify it by barcode scan against the expected item, or (b) force an independent second-user verification with its own authentication before the step can be completed. The verifier must be a different user from the performer (system-enforced), and both identities, timestamps and the verified value are stored. Verifier: option (a) removes the manual entry rather than checking it - acceptable and usually preferable, but the interface then falls under §5 and must be validated (§4).
note: No change.

requirement: Data must be protected against damage by both physical and electronic means; stored data must be verified as accessible, readable and accurate; and access to the data must be assured throughout the retention period.
system_implications: Database and file storage must sit on protected, redundant infrastructure; the system should provide integrity checking (e.g., record-level hashes or database consistency checks) and a retrievability check that proves old batch records can still be opened and rendered with their audit trail and signatures. Retention rules per record type (EU batch documentation: at least one year beyond expiry or five years after QP certification, whichever is longer, per EU GMP Chapter 4) must be configurable and must block premature deletion.
note: No change (the retention rule quoted in the implications is correctly attributed to Ch.4 4.11).

requirement: All relevant data must be backed up regularly, and backups must be shown to be complete, accurate and restorable - first during validation and then through periodic monitoring.
system_implications: Backups must cover the database, attachments, configuration (recipes/master batch records, user/role definitions) and audit trails as a consistent set. Restore procedures must be documented and exercised; the system should log backup job success/failure and alert on failure. Point-in-time recovery objectives should be set by risk (an injectable line running continuous aseptic filling needs a tight recovery point so in-progress batch data are not lost). Verifier: backup alerts and recovery-point objectives are design choices set by risk (§1, §16).
note: No change.

requirement: The system must be able to produce clear paper copies of data it stores electronically, and for records that support batch release it must be able to print a version indicating whether any value was changed since first entry.
system_implications: The eBMR needs a controlled print/export of the executed batch record (human-readable, complete, paginated, with unique record ID, version and 'page x of y') in which every value that was modified after first entry is visibly flagged, ideally with original value, new value, who, when and why, or a cross-reference to the audit trail entry. The rendered copy must also show signatures with name, date/time and meaning. Verifier: §8.2 requires the ability to generate a printout that indicates changed data; showing signer name and meaning reflects 21 CFR 11.50 (Annex 11 §14 itself requires date/time and permanent linkage); pagination and record ID are good practice.
note: No change.

requirement: Where the system exchanges data electronically with other systems, suitable built-in checks must ensure the data are entered and processed correctly and securely, so as to reduce risk.
system_implications: Every interface (ERP/material status, LIMS results, balances, PLC/SCADA, historian, label printing, QMS deviations) must validate what it receives: message schema and completeness, identity matching (material code, lot, batch ID), unit and range checks, duplicate/sequence detection, acknowledgement and retry, and authenticated/encrypted transport. Failed or rejected transfers must raise a visible alert and must never silently drop or default a value into the batch record. Verifier: authenticated/encrypted transport is security good practice (supports §12) rather than a §5 requirement.
note: No change (the line's 'corruption or loss' wording is a harmless gloss on 'risks').

requirement: Based on a risk assessment, building into the system an automatically generated audit trail of every GMP-relevant change or deletion should be considered. When GMP-relevant data are changed or deleted, the reason must be documented. Audit trails must be retrievable, convertible into a form people can generally understand, and reviewed at regular intervals. (For an eBMR holding batch-release data the risk assessment will in practice conclude that an audit trail is needed.)
system_implications: Every create/modify/delete of GMP data in the eBMR (step results, parameters, material entries, comments, status changes, signatures, voids) must write an append-only, system-generated entry holding user ID and full name, date/time with time zone, record/field identity, old value, new value and a mandatory reason (reason list plus free text). Ordinary users and administrators must not be able to edit, delete or switch off the trail; the trail must be viewable and exportable in plain language (not only raw database codes), filterable by batch, and flagged for review. Verifier: the 2011 §9 makes the audit trail risk-based (consideration should be given); for an eBMR the risk assessment should conclude it is required, and EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity expects it. Blocking administrators from editing or disabling the trail, full-name and time-zone capture, and logging record creation go beyond the 2011 text (EMA Q&A, PIC/S PI 041, 2025 draft revision of Annex 11) - still implement. Keeping the old value is also required by Ch.4 4.9.
note: MODERATE correction: 2011 §9 says an audit trail should be CONSIDERED on the basis of risk; the line stated it as an unconditional 'the system should generate'. The reason-for-change and the availability, intelligibility and regular-review parts are firm. The eBMR should still implement a full, always-on audit trail (EMA Q&A expectation).

requirement: Any change to a computerised system, configuration included, may be made only in a controlled way that follows a defined procedure.
system_implications: Master batch records/recipes, workflows, calculations, limits, role definitions and interface settings must be version-controlled objects with draft-review-approve-effective states, e-signed approvals, and an audit trail of configuration changes. Only one effective version per product and batch size (processing) or per product, pack size and type (packaging) may be usable for new batches; in-flight batches must stay bound to the version they started on unless an approved change says otherwise. Software releases must go through a test environment before production. Verifier: master batch records are also GMP instruction documents, so their approval and versioning derive from Ch.4 4.3/4.5 and their change-control records from Ch.4 4.29, in addition to §10. Testing releases in a test environment first is good practice (§4.7 refers to test environments).
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: the 'one effective version' rule scoped per product and batch size / pack size and type.

requirement: Computerised systems must be evaluated periodically to confirm they are still in a validated state and GMP-compliant; where relevant the review considers the system's current functions, its deviation, incident and problem history, the upgrades made, how it has performed and how reliable and secure it has been, and its validation status.
system_implications: The eBMR should make periodic review easy by providing reports for the review period: configuration and software changes, incident/error logs, interface failures, user-access changes and privileged activity, backup/restore results, performance/uptime, open validation gaps. System-generated reports are preferable for reliability, but §11 does not require the evidence to be system-generated.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: system-generated evidence relabelled as a preference.

requirement: Physical and/or logical controls must limit system access to authorised persons (examples include physical keys or badges, individual passwords, biometrics and locking away hardware and storage); how strong the controls are depends on how critical the system is; and granting, changing and withdrawing access rights must be recorded.
system_implications: Individual named accounts with role-based permissions (operator, verifier/witness, supervisor, QA reviewer, QP, master-data author, administrator); user administration workflow that logs every grant/change/revocation with requester, approver, date and reason; history of who held which role on any past date must be queryable. Shop-floor terminals in cleanrooms (injectables, Grade A/B gowned operators) need an authentication method usable with gloves (badge/RFID + PIN or biometrics) without resorting to shared logins. Verifier: §12.3 requires access changes to be recorded; requester/approver/reason fields and point-in-time role history are good practice. Individual named accounts are implied by §12.4 (identity of the operator) and explicit in EMA GMP Q&A / PIC/S PI 041.
note: No change.

requirement: Systems managing data and documents must capture who entered, changed, confirmed or deleted each item of data, and when (date and time).
system_implications: Each recorded value and each confirmation (e.g., 'performed', 'verified', 'checked') must carry the authenticated user identity and a trusted server timestamp (not a client-device clock the operator can change). Timestamps should be synchronised to a reliable time source and stored with time-zone information so multi-site data line up. Verifier: deletions must be attributed too (§12.4 covers deleting); the time source and time-zone storage are design means.
note: No change.

requirement: Every incident, including but not limited to system failures and data errors, must be reported and evaluated; for critical incidents the root cause must be determined and must drive corrective and preventive action.
system_implications: The eBMR must log technical and functional incidents (interface failures, lost connections, crashes during a step, failed signatures, time-sync failures, printing failures) in a way that links them to affected batches, so an incident can be raised in the QMS and its batch impact assessed before release. Batches touched by an open incident should be flagged on the release/QP view. Verifier: batch linkage and QP-view flags go beyond §13 but support Ch.4 4.27 (a system to indicate special observations). §13 also requires root-cause analysis feeding CAPA for critical incidents - the incident record should hold a criticality rating and a CAPA link.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: added root cause and CAPA linkage.

requirement: Electronic records may be signed electronically. Such signatures are expected to carry, within the company, the same weight as handwritten ones, to stay permanently tied to the record they sign, and to show the date and time they were applied.
system_implications: Signing must require the signer's own credentials at the moment of signing; the signature object (user ID, printed full name, date/time with zone, meaning such as performed/verified/reviewed/approved/certified) must be stored bound to the exact record version (e.g., via record hash), must display on screen and on every rendered copy, and cannot be copied, moved or re-used on another record. A company policy/attestation that users accept e-signatures as equivalent to handwritten ones should be captured in the system (acknowledgement at account activation). Verifier: printed name, signature meaning and credential entry at each signing reflect 21 CFR Part 11 (11.50, 11.200); Annex 11 §14 asks for equal effect to handwritten signatures inside the company, permanent linkage and date/time - keep the Part 11 elements for dual-market use. Equal effect inside the company is primarily a company policy; user acknowledgement is one way to evidence it.
note: No change.

requirement: If a computerised system records batch certification and release, it must let only Qualified Persons certify batch release, must clearly identify and record who released or certified each batch, and this must be done by electronic signature.
system_implications: A distinct 'QP certification' permission, granted only to persons named as QP on the manufacturing/import authorisation (with an approval workflow and a register of QP accounts). Certification is an e-signature with the meaning 'certified by QP' and the QP's identity; release status changes (quarantine to certified/released) must be possible only through this action and must feed downstream systems (ERP/warehouse) to lift quarantine. Other users, including admins and QA reviewers without QP status, must not be able to certify. Verifier: feeding ERP/warehouse status from the certification is a design choice beyond §15.
note: No change.

requirement: Where computerised systems support critical processes, provisions such as a manual or alternative system must keep those processes going if the system breaks down; how quickly the fallback must be available is set by risk and by the system and process concerned; and the arrangements must be adequately documented and tested.
system_implications: Provide a validated downtime mode: controlled pre-printed/printable emergency batch record sheets generated from the current master record (uniquely numbered, reconciled), local buffering on the shop floor for short network outages with guaranteed ordered re-sync, and a controlled back-entry procedure after recovery where late-entered data are flagged as transcribed from paper, second-person verified, and linked to the scanned original. Injectables: an aseptic filling run cannot simply stop, so fallback must be immediate and pre-staged; tablets may tolerate a planned pause at defined hold points. Verifier: §16 requires the arrangements to be documented and tested; calling it a 'validated' mode goes further (reasonable for injectables). Back-entry of transcribed data is manual entry of critical data, so Annex 11 §6 accuracy checks apply.
note: No change.

requirement: Data may be archived; archived data must be verified as accessible, readable and intact, and when relevant changes to the system (e.g., hardware or programs) are planned, the ability to retrieve the archived data must be ensured and tested.
system_implications: Archive function that moves completed, released batch records (with full audit trail, signatures, attachments and metadata) into read-only storage, with fixity checks (hashes) run periodically and a restore/re-render capability that still works after application upgrades. Upgrade validation must include retrieval tests of archived records from earlier versions. Verifier: §17 sets no frequency for the checks; periodic fixity checking is a design choice. Archiving must also cover rejected and non-released batch records, not only released ones.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: archiving scope extended to non-released batches.

requirement: Process owner, system owner, QPs, IT and other relevant staff must cooperate closely, and all personnel need appropriate qualifications, access level and defined responsibilities (§2). Formal agreements stating the third party's responsibilities are required whenever a third party is involved in supplying, setting up, integrating, validating, maintaining (including by remote access), changing or hosting/retaining the system, or in processing data; internal IT departments are to be treated the same way (§3.1). Supplier competence and reliability are key selection factors and the need for an audit is decided by risk (§3.2). Quality-system and audit information on software and system suppliers or developers must be made available to inspectors on request (§3.4).
system_implications: Roles for process owner and system owner should be configurable in the system and shown on validation/periodic review outputs. For a SaaS or vendor-hosted eBMR: a quality/technical agreement covering data ownership, backup, change notification, incident reporting, audit-trail retention, access for inspections and exit/data return; the vendor should support customer audits and provide release notes and validation packages. Verifier: agreements are also needed with internal IT or group shared-service IT running the infrastructure or application (§3.1 treats IT departments like third parties), and with validation contractors, remote-maintenance providers and archive/retention providers. Showing owner roles in the application is a design choice.
note: MINOR correction: the line narrowed the agreement requirement to parties that 'supply or run' the system; §3.1 also covers integration, validation, remote maintenance, modification, retention and data processing, and treats internal IT departments like third parties.

requirement: User requirements must describe the functions the system needs, rest on a documented risk assessment and GMP-impact analysis, and stay traceable through the life cycle. Validation must evidence appropriate test methods and scenarios, paying special attention to limits on process parameters, limits on data values and how errors are handled; automated test tools and test environments need documented assessments of their adequacy.
system_implications: Maintain a URS-to-test traceability matrix for the system (§4.4); verifying each configured product/recipe is good practice beyond §4.4. The eBMR must enforce configured limits (warning vs action/reject limits for weights, in-process results, CPPs) and must handle errors deterministically (e.g., instrument disconnect, invalid barcode, double submission) - all of which must be tested, including boundary values. If automated/regression testing tools are used, keep an assessment of their fitness.
note: No change to the requirement. Implications: per-recipe traceability relabelled as beyond the clause.

requirement: Documents may be partly paper and partly electronic; for hybrid and single-medium systems the company must state how masters, controlled copies, data processing and records relate and how each is controlled.
system_implications: The eBMR configuration must define which object is the master (the approved electronic master batch record/recipe), which outputs are official copies (controlled PDFs/prints, watermarked 'copy' with generation date and version), and which is the original record of execution (the electronic record with its audit trail). Any remaining paper elements (e.g., printed labels, instrument printouts, EM plates) need a defined link to the electronic batch (scan + reconciliation + reference ID). Verifier: merge the controlled-copy marking detail into EU4-08.
note: Same point as EU4-08 (4.1 hybrid systems); also duplicated by C4-05 (intl-india-who-ich). Paraphrase faithful. Unique content to merge: copy marking with version and generation date (good practice).

requirement: Batch documentation must be kept until one year after batch expiry or at least five years after QP certification, whichever ends later.
system_implications: Retention end date must be computed per batch as the later of (expiry + 1 year) and (QP certification date + 5 years), be longer if other markets or company policy require it, and block purge/archiving-with-deletion before that date. Audit trails, signatures and metadata inherit the same retention as the batch record. Verifier: see EU4-15 for the investigational-product rule and product-specific longer periods.
note: Same point as EU4-15; this line omits the investigational-product and product-specific retention rules that EU4-15 includes.

requirement: Records must be made or completed when each action is taken; alterations must be signed and dated, keep the original readable and, where appropriate, give the reason.
system_implications: Entry screens must record the actual execution time automatically; entries made materially later than the step (configurable threshold) are flagged as late with a mandatory justification. Corrections never overwrite: the prior value stays visible in history and on the review/print rendering, and the correction carries user e-signature, timestamp and reason. No 'edit in place' for executed steps without this correction workflow. Verifier: the configurable late-entry threshold with justification is good practice, not stated in 4.8.
note: Same points as EU4-12 and EU4-13 (also duplicated by C4-03 in intl-india-who-ich). Paraphrase faithful; the researcher's verified=false can be treated as verified.

requirement: Regulated users must review the documentation that comes with COTS products to confirm it satisfies their user requirements (§3.3). The validation file should contain change-control records (if any) and reports of deviations observed during validation (§4.2). The regulated user must make every reasonable effort to confirm the system was built under a suitable quality management system, and must assess the supplier appropriately (§4.5). For bespoke or customised systems, a process must formally assess and report quality and performance metrics at every life-cycle stage (§4.6).
system_implications: eBMR vendors should provide a validation package (requirements, design/configuration specs, test evidence, release notes, known-issues list) and evidence of their development QMS (SDLC, code review, testing, defect management). Customer-specific extensions (custom scripts, reports, interfaces) must be treated as bespoke and carry their own lifecycle quality metrics and test evidence. Validation deviations must be recorded and reported (§4.2); resolving or formally justifying them before go-live is good practice.
note: No change; the researcher's verified=false can be treated as verified. Nuance: change-control records are required only if applicable. Implications: 'resolved before release' relabelled as good practice.

clause: Annex 11 §9; §8.2. Pre-release review of critical-data changes: EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity / PIC/S PI 041 (nearest 2011 anchors: Ch.4 4.27 and the regular-review wording of §9)
requirement: On a risk basis, a system-generated audit trail of GMP-relevant changes and deletions should be considered; reasons for changing or deleting GMP-relevant data must be documented; audit trails must be available, intelligible and regularly reviewed; and for records supporting batch release it must be possible to print a version showing whether data changed since first entry. Assessing changes to critical data before release is an EMA Q&A / PIC/S expectation; in the 2011 texts it is anchored only by Ch.4 4.27 (a system flagging changes to critical data for release) and by §9's regular review.
system_implications: The system keeps an immutable audit trail of who, what, when, old value, new value and reason for every create, modify, delete, void, status change and signature on batch data. A reason is mandatory for any change to a committed GMP value. The batch review screen and release printout have a clear 'data changed after entry' indicator for each changed value, plus a batch-scoped, human-readable audit-trail report filtered to GMP-relevant events on critical data. Audit-trail review is a signed, mandatory step in batch review, and release (or QP certification) is blocked until it is done. Audit trails cannot be switched off by users. Verifier: the signed audit-trail review that gates release, and the rule that audit trails cannot be switched off, come from EMA GMP Q&A (data integrity) and PIC/S PI 041, not the 2011 texts - keep as best practice. §8.2 requires that such a printout can be generated, not that every printout carries the indicator.
note: DUPLICATE, with the same MODERATE §9 overstatement as A11-10 (pics). PART NOT IN REGULATION: the pre-release audit-trail review comes from EMA GMP Q&A / PIC/S PI 041 - keep it as a separate best-practice requirement when merging.
duplicate_of: A11-10 + A11-08 (intl-annex11-pics.jsonl); pre-release review element overlaps EU4-17

clause: Ch.4 4.20(a)-(i) and Note; the 'avoid transcription errors' idea is 4.2 in the 2011 text
requirement: Same content as EU4-04 and EU4-05: a processing record for each batch based on the currently approved formula and instructions with the 4.20 content, plus the Note permitting summary and exception reporting for validated, continuously monitored processes. The 2011 text of 4.20 has no sentence on designing record preparation to avoid transcription errors (that matches the pre-2011 wording); the 2011 equivalent is 4.2, which bars reproduction from masters from introducing errors.
system_implications: The executable batch record is generated automatically from the effective, approved MBR version, with no re-keying of instructions. Its version ID appears on every page and in the output. Mandatory structured fields cover all the content groups above, with server-side timestamps for start, key stages and finish, and user identity for performer and checker (checker must be a different person). Material lots and actual weights come from dispensing and scanning. Equipment IDs are scanned with status checks. Yield calculations are automatic at defined stages with alert limits. Any departure needs a deviation record with signed authorisation (4.20(h)); requiring QA specifically is a company choice (Ch.5 5.15: competent person, QC involved where appropriate). Final production approval is by e-signature from the responsible role. For continuously monitored automated steps (for example a tablet press with automated weight control, or an isolator filling line with integrated monitoring), the record may store a validated compliance summary plus exceptions, while the full data stay retrievable. Verifier: merge into EU4-04 the unique points - checker must differ from performer, MBR version on every page, yield alert limits.
note: DUPLICATE with MINOR correction: the transcription-error point was attributed to 4.20 but in the 2011 text it is 4.2. Implications: QA-only deviation authorisation relabelled as a company choice.

clause: Ch.4 4.21(a)-(i); the electronic-controls exemption sits inside 4.21(h) only
requirement: Same content as EU4-06 and EU4-07. Correction: the robust-electronic-controls justification applies only to the reconciliation information in 4.21(h), not to any other packaging-record content.
system_implications: The packaging record has line-clearance checks (signed and verified) before start. Printed components are issued and returned by barcode scan with lot IDs and counts. Coding and overprint text (batch, expiry and, where used, serialisation data) is captured as an image or data specimen and verified against expected values. Vision and reject-station counts come from the line. Automatic reconciliation compares issued, used, destroyed and returned counts with limits, and any breach becomes a deviation. Any MBR decision to omit the reconciliation data (the only content 4.21(h) allows to be omitted) because of electronic controls must reference the validated control and a risk assessment. Tablets: blister or bottle lines. Injectables: vial or ampoule labelling and cartoning after visual inspection. Verifier: reconciliation limits with a deviation on breach reflect Ch.5 5.61 (EU5-17), beyond Ch.4.
note: DUPLICATE with MODERATE correction: the line suggested electronic controls could justify leaving out 'some of this detail, such as reconciliation'; in the text the justification is placed within item (h) and covers only the reconciliation data.

requirement: Records must be made or completed as each action is done so that significant activities are traceable; alterations must be signed and dated, keep the original readable and, where appropriate, state the reason.
system_implications: Timestamps come from a synchronised server clock, not the client device. Each entry records who did the action and when, and the system flags entries made more than a configured interval after the step's actual execution (late entries), requiring a reason and showing them in the exception report. Corrections never overwrite: the original stays visible in the record view and the printout, and the correction stores user, time and a mandatory reason chosen from a controlled list plus optional free text. Back-dating is impossible.
note: Same as EU4-12 + EU4-13 and C4-05 (intl-annex11-pics). Paraphrase faithful.

clause: Ch.4 4.10; 4.11; 4.12 (the validation raw-data and MA-support retention points are 4.12, not 4.10/4.11)
requirement: Same content as EU4-14, EU4-15 and EU4-16: record-to-activity mapping and integrity controls (4.10), batch documentation retention (4.11), and retention of critical MA-supporting documentation and validation raw data (4.12).
system_implications: Each batch record (including audit trail, signatures, attachments, exception reports and linked deviations) gets a computed retention date: the later of expiry plus 1 year and QP certification date plus 5 years, extended by any configured longer rule (market law, validation linkage, clinical use). Deletion or purge before that date is technically blocked. Archive and migration keep the record readable with its metadata and audit trail, and are verified. Validation datasets are linked to the batches they support, so their retention extends automatically. A record-location register shows where each record type is held. Verifier: the validation-linkage and MA-support retention points derive from 4.12.
note: DUPLICATE with MINOR clause correction: 4.12 was omitted from the citation although the line paraphrases it.

requirement: Same content as EU4-08 and EU4-09: any medium or hybrid; stated relationships and controls between masters, copies, data and records; controlled electronic templates; error-free reproduction from masters; approved, signed and dated instructions.
system_implications: For every record type, the system configuration or SOP register states which form is the official (master) record: electronic, paper or defined hybrid parts. MBRs (masters) are approved by e-signature of the authorised roles (for example production, QA and, where required, regulatory) before becoming effective. Executed batch records are generated from the master by the system, never retyped. Any printed copy carries 'copy' status, the source version and the print time, and cannot be used as the official record unless issued through the controlled-form route (see EMA-DI-05). Verifier: EMA-DI-05 is not in this input set; the controlled-form issuance route is EMA data-integrity Q&A / PIC/S PI 041 practice rather than Ch.4 text.
note: Same as EU4-08 + EU4-09 (and C4-01 in intl-annex11-pics). Paraphrase faithful.

requirement: Same content as A11-16 and A11-17: e-signatures with the same effect as handwritten ones inside the company, permanently linked and dated/timed; only QPs may certify release in a system that records it, identified and recorded, by e-signature.
system_implications: Each e-signature is cryptographically or relationally bound to the exact record version signed and shows the signer's name, date, time and meaning (performed, verified, reviewed, approved, certified). Editing signed content invalidates the signature and requires re-signing. The certify/release action is available only to users holding the QP role (EU) or the authorised QA-release role (US), is checked at execution time, and records the signer. Release is blocked while open items remain (see Q10-03 and A11-01). Verifier: invalidating a signature when signed content changes is a design reading of 'permanently linked'; showing name and meaning reflects 21 CFR 11.50. Q10-03 is not in this input set.
note: Same as A11-16 + A11-17 (intl-annex11-pics). Paraphrase faithful.

requirement: Same content as A11-09 and A11-05: built-in checks on electronically exchanged data, and an additional accuracy check (second person or validated electronic means) for critical data entered by hand, scoped by risk.
system_implications: Field-level validation covers type, range, format and unit. Barcode or RFID identity checks cover materials, equipment, rooms and containers, and a mismatch prevents the step from continuing. Interface transfers (ERP material master, LIMS results, scales, SCADA/historian) use checksums or acknowledgments with reconciliation, and failed transfers raise alerts. Any critical value keyed in by hand, as determined by the field's criticality attribute (see EMA-DI-02), requires independent second-person verification by e-signature, unless a validated electronic check covers it (for example a direct balance interface). Tablet examples: API potency-adjusted quantity, granulation fluid amount. Injectable examples: compounding volumes, filter-integrity test values typed from an off-line tester, sterilisation load IDs. Verifier: EMA-DI-02 (field criticality attribute) is not in this input set; field criticality should be traceable to the §1/§6 risk assessment.
note: Same as A11-09 + A11-05 (intl-annex11-pics). 'Transferred' is a harmless gloss on §5's entry and processing.

clause: Annex 11 §12.1-§12.4 (the cited §4.8/§5 do not match this content); role-based access, unique IDs and admin segregation: EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity / PIC/S PI 041, partly anchored by Annex 11 §2 (appropriate level of access)
requirement: Same content as A11-13 and A11-14 for access restriction, criticality-based controls, recording of access changes and attribution of data actions. Unique user identity is implied by §12.4; role-based access partly by §2; separating administrator rights from GMP data entry is not in the 2011 text (EMA Q&A / PIC/S expectation).
system_implications: Every account belongs to one named person, with no shared or generic GMP accounts. Roles are role-based (operator, verifier, supervisor, QA reviewer, QP/QA release, MBR author, MBR approver, system administrator). Separation of duties is enforced: administrators cannot sign GMP steps, MBR authors cannot approve their own MBRs, and performers cannot verify their own entries. Account and role changes are logged and reviewed periodically, with the review recorded. Sessions lock after inactivity, and signing requires re-entry of credentials. Verifier: separation of duties, periodic access review and session locking are best practice from EMA GMP Q&A / PIC/S PI 041 (and the 2025 draft revision of Annex 11), not the 2011 text; performer-versus-verifier independence is inherent in §6 (second operator). Keep all.
note: DUPLICATE with MINOR clause correction (irrelevant §4.8/§5 citation). PART NOT IN REGULATION: administrator segregation / separation of duties comes from EMA GMP Q&A and PIC/S PI 041 - keep as a best-practice requirement when merging.

clause: Ch.4 preamble 'Required GMP documentation' - Records (raw data)
requirement: Records include the raw data from which other records are generated. For electronic records the regulated user must define which data count as raw data, and as a minimum every data item on which a quality decision is based must be defined as raw data.
system_implications: Maintain a raw-data classification per master and per data field (e.g., raw / derived / informational) under change control; as a minimum, every value feeding a quality decision (weights, IPC results, CPP readings, yields, reconciliation counts, alarms used in review-by-exception, EM results used for release) is raw data. Raw data are retained unaltered with metadata and audit trail for the batch retention period, including data captured from PLC/SCADA, historians and instruments that the eBMR only summarises (compliance summaries under the 4.20 Note must not replace them). Derived values keep their inputs and the calculation version.
verification_test: Inspect the raw-data register for one tablet and one injectable master: every field used in an IPC, yield/reconciliation or release decision is classified raw. For a summarised parameter (e.g., fill weight trend or compression force), retrieve the underlying raw data for the batch. Recompute a derived value from its stored inputs and confirm it matches.

clause: Ch.4 preamble 'Required GMP documentation' - instruction type (manufacturing formulae, processing, packaging and testing instructions)
requirement: Manufacturing formulae and processing, packaging and testing instructions must spell out every starting material, item of equipment and computerised system (if any) to be used, and give complete instructions for processing, packaging, sampling and testing; where relevant they must also name the in-process controls and process analytical technology (PAT) to be applied, with acceptance criteria.
system_implications: Each master step names the computerised systems it relies on (e.g., the eBMR itself, PLC/SCADA recipe and version, weighing system, checkweigher, vision/serialisation system, autoclave or lyophiliser controller, filter-integrity tester), so the batch record shows which validated system and version produced the data. Where PAT is used (e.g., NIR blend uniformity for tablets, in-line checks on injectable lines), the master defines the PAT method, model version and acceptance criteria and the record captures the result against them. Sampling steps carry their sampling instructions.
verification_test: Review a master: every step using an automated system names that system and its approved version/recipe; a PAT step without acceptance criteria cannot be approved; executing a batch records the system/recipe version actually used and flags any mismatch with the master.

requirement: Instructions must be error-free and must be available in written, human-readable form.
system_implications: Before a master is approved its content is independently verified (quantities and units, limits, calculation formulas, equipment classes, step order), ideally supported by automated consistency checks (BOM total against batch size, units consistent, limits within registered ranges). Operators can always see the current instruction text at each step, including during downtime via the Annex 11 §16 fallback (printable instructions generated from the effective master).
verification_test: Seed a draft master with a unit error and a limit outside the registered range: the automated checks or the verification step catch both before approval. Confirm each executing step displays its instruction text and that a printable version is available in downtime mode.

clause: Ch.4 preamble 'Required GMP documentation' - Certificates of Analysis, footnote 1
requirement: Where the marketing authorisation provides for it (real-time release testing), certification can be based fully or partly on evaluating summaries and exception reports of real-time batch data from PAT or from process parameters and metrics, instead of end-product test results.
system_implications: Conditional - only if RTRT/PAT-based release is in the MA: the eBMR generates, per batch, a validated summary and exception report of the PAT/parameter data the MA specifies, linked to the MA reference and model version, available to the QP for certification, with the underlying raw data retained (EUA-NEW-01). Not applicable otherwise.
verification_test: For an RTRT product, run a batch with one PAT excursion: the summary shows compliance per registered attribute, the excursion appears in the exception report and is visible to the QP before certification, and the underlying spectra/parameter data are retrievable.

requirement: Approved, dated specifications must exist for starting materials, packaging materials and finished products, and specifications for intermediate and bulk products must be available for critical steps or when such products are bought in or dispatched. Material specifications include how materials are stored and how long they can be held before re-testing; finished-product specifications include the formula, dosage form and pack, storage and handling needs, and shelf-life.
system_implications: Master data reference the current approved specification version for the product (4.17(a)) and for each packaging component (4.19(d)); a new specification version triggers an impact assessment on the masters. At dispensing the eBMR checks the lot is released and within its re-test or expiry date (enforcement itself is Ch.5 5.34, see EU5-27). Hold points at critical steps, and bulk dispatched to another site (e.g., bulk tablets to a packager, bulk solution to a filling site), apply the approved intermediate/bulk specification limits. The expiry date recorded and printed on packs is calculated from the shelf-life in the effective finished-product specification using a defined start-of-shelf-life rule.
verification_test: Try to dispense a lot past its re-test date - blocked. In a test system change the finished-product shelf-life and confirm new batches use the new value only once the specification is effective. Dispatch a bulk batch and confirm its record shows results against the approved bulk specification.

requirement: Every incoming delivery - starting materials of any kind (bulk, intermediates and finished goods included) and all primary, secondary and printed packaging materials - must be received under a written procedure and recorded. Receipt records must let each received lot be identified (external and internal names or codes, supplier and manufacturer with the manufacturer's batch number, and the internal batch number assigned on receipt) and quantified (total quantity, number of containers and date received), with room for relevant remarks.
system_implications: Where the eBMR/MES suite handles goods receipt it captures these data and assigns the internal lot number. In all cases the lot scanned at dispensing or at packaging-material issue must resolve to its receipt record (supplier, manufacturer and manufacturer's batch), giving genealogy from supplier lot to finished batch for traceability (4.8) and recall. Bulk or intermediates received from another site are received like starting materials.
verification_test: From a finished batch, trace an API lot and a printed carton lot back to receipt records showing manufacturer and manufacturer's batch number. Attempt to issue a lot that has no receipt record - blocked.

requirement: Written procedures must govern how starting materials, packaging materials and, as appropriate, other materials are labelled internally, held in quarantine and stored.
system_implications: Labels the eBMR prints for dispensed materials, intermediates and bulk containers (content, lot, quantity, status, hold/expiry date, storage condition) follow approved, version-controlled templates defined under that procedure. The eBMR displays and respects material status (quarantine, released, rejected) and prevents use of quarantined or rejected material (the use prohibition itself is Ch.5); status changes are e-signed and audit-trailed.
verification_test: Print a dispensing label and an intermediate container label and confirm template version and mandatory fields. Try to use a quarantined intermediate in a following step - blocked. Release it with a QA e-signature and confirm the step can then proceed.

requirement: Sampling must follow written procedures that set the method, equipment and amount to take and the precautions against contaminating or degrading the material; testing of materials and products at the different manufacturing stages must follow written procedures describing methods and equipment, and the tests performed must be recorded; and clear operating procedures must be available for major manufacturing and test equipment.
system_implications: Sampling and IPC steps reference the governing procedure and version and show the amount to take, sampling tool and precautions (aseptic sampling precautions for sterile products); sample IDs and quantities withdrawn are recorded so they enter yield and reconciliation. Every test performed in production (IPC or at-line) is recorded with result, method reference and performer, including repeat tests, which are added as new results rather than overwriting. Steps operating major equipment link to the current effective operating procedure.
verification_test: Execute a sampling step: the record shows procedure/version, sample ID, quantity taken and sampler. Repeat an IPC test: both results are visible. The equipment procedure link opens the current effective version.

requirement: Written procedures and associated records are required for personnel matters, including signature lists, GMP and technical training (and checks that it was effective), and gowning and hygiene; Annex 11 §2 requires personnel to have appropriate qualifications for their assigned duties.
system_implications: Maintain an electronic signature register linking each user ID to full name, initials if used, roles, permitted signature types and validity dates, retained as long as any record that user signed. Integrate training records so users can perform or verify only steps for which their training is current (training gating is good practice rather than an explicit Ch.4 rule). For injectables, aseptic-area steps can require current gowning qualification.
verification_test: Resolve any signer on an archived batch record to full name and role valid on the signing date. Expire a user's training for a step and confirm the system blocks that user from performing it, with the block audit-trailed.

clause: Ch.4 4.29 (validation and qualification, change control, deviations and non-conformances, complaints, recalls, returns, record summaries such as product quality review); 4.27
requirement: Policies, procedures, protocols, reports and records of actions or conclusions are required for quality processes that touch batches - among them validation and qualification, change control, investigation of deviations and non-conformances, complaints, recalls and returns - and for record summaries where appropriate, such as the product quality review.
system_implications: Each batch record links to the deviations/investigations raised on it, to the change control behind its master version, and to later complaints, returns or recalls involving it; master versions reference their change-control record and supporting validation; batches made under a validation or study protocol are flagged and linked to that protocol. Provide a structured export of batch data for product quality review (yields, IPC trends, deviations, reconciliation results, changes) so PQR summaries are drawn from source records rather than re-keyed.
verification_test: From a batch, open its linked deviations and the change control of its master version; from a complaint, find the batch record. Export PQR data for a product over a period and reconcile totals against the individual batch records.

clause: Ch.4 4.29 (environmental monitoring); 4.27 (all records available to the QP)
requirement: Written procedures and records are required for environmental monitoring, and every record relevant to a batch must be available to the QP.
system_implications: Injectables: the batch record links the environmental and personnel monitoring results for the rooms/Grade A zones and time window of aseptic processing and shows open excursions to the QP before certification (batch-linked EM review detail comes from Annex 1, beyond Ch.4). Tablets: EM records may stay outside the eBMR, but rooms and times used must be traceable so the relevant EM data can be retrieved.
verification_test: For an aseptic fill, open the batch review and confirm the EM results for the filling room and time window are linked, and that an open EM excursion is flagged on the QP screen.

requirement: The quality management system must keep a maintained list (inventory) of its documents.
system_implications: The eBMR can list all its controlled documents - processing and packaging masters, templates, forms, label templates, embedded work instructions - with ID, version, status, effective date and next review date, for inclusion in or synchronisation with the site document inventory.
verification_test: Generate the list and reconcile it with the site document inventory: every effective master/template appears once, with matching version and status.

requirement: Validation documentation and reports must cover the relevant steps of the system life cycle, and the manufacturer must be able to defend, from its risk assessment, the validation approach it chose - the standards and protocols used, the acceptance criteria, and the procedures and records produced.
system_implications: The eBMR validation package spans the life cycle from requirements through operation to retirement, including configuration of master/recipe types, interfaces, calculations, reports and data migration, with a documented risk rationale for test depth; new masters and configuration changes are verified under the same approach. Plan retirement (data retention and readability after decommissioning) as part of the life cycle.
verification_test: Review the validation plan and report: they cover requirements through operation and retirement, cite the risk assessment for test depth, and include verification of a sample of configured masters.
